plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MUU) to zero for capital preservation.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets approximately 1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It aims for steady, low-drawdown performance by significantly reducing leverage and concentrating on broad market exposure. Expect lower volatility but also limited upside potential.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MUU) to small allocations.
Reduce QQQI to 20% to comply with the single name concentration mandate.
Buy ZS, a top-quality scanner setup, to add growth potential.
This approach balances risk and growth, maintaining a moderate cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets approximately 2.5% per month, prioritizing risk-first growth. It blends broad index exposure with quality tech and a small amount of leverage. Expect moderate volatility and growth potential, with a focus on managing overall portfolio risk.

plan: Add to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MUU) to increase exposure.
Increase positions in leveraged AI/Software (PLTU, MSFU) for growth.
Buy ZS, a high-scoring scanner setup, to concentrate in strong trends.
Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
This plan uses leverage and concentration to target aggressive growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets approximately 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It leans into leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups, which significantly raises both upside and drawdown potential. Be aware that leveraged ETFs decay daily, and this approach can lead to substantial losses quickly if stops are not strictly adhered to.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MUU) to zero.
Sell high-beta single names (PLTU, MSFU) to near zero.
Add to QQQI, increasing income-focused ETF exposure.
Add to SPY for broad market stability and reduced volatility.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan targets approximately 1% per month, aiming to park cash for yield. It rotates into income-focused ETFs and broad index exposure, cutting leverage and high-beta names. While prioritizing low drawdown and reliable income, remember distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
